chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abd al-Rahman al-Abzari al-Kunasi, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What is your view if a man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'By Allah, I do not know whether you are a Prophet or not,' would he accept from him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but he would kill him. Indeed, if he had accepted that from him, no hypocrite would ever become a Muslim.'
ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet kill those who said 'I do not know if you are a prophet' instead of accepting their statement?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the criterion for accepting a convert's declaration of faith, emphasizing that mere verbal assertion without genuine conviction is insufficient. He illustrates this by noting that if the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his progeny) had accepted such uncertainty, hypocrites (*munafiqun*) could easily feign Islam while concealing disbelief, thereby nullifying the sincerity required for true entry into the religion. This underscores the Shia scholarly view that *ikhlas* (sincerity) is intrinsic to the validity of the testimony of faith, linking the legal penalty for apostasy to the prevention of hypocrisy.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abul Rahman Al Abzary Al Kunasy, from Al Haris Bin Al Mugheira who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What is your<sup>asws</sup> view if a man came to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, so he said, ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I do not know whether you<sup>saww</sup> are a Prophet<sup>saww</sup> or not, would he<sup>saww</sup> have accepted from him?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No! But, he<sup>saww</sup> would have killed him. If he<sup>saww</sup> had accepted from him, no hypocrite would ever become a Muslim’.
